scope: Expectations/execution perspective kept analytically separate from discovery. Existing TER and SERV T0 packets only; no price-derived score, rank, membership or methodology mutation.
summary: Execution evidence is directionally constructive for both active names but remains insufficient to close their gating underwriting packets. Teradyne continues to position test coverage across the AI device chain and is building M&A execution capacity; that raises the burden on current capital-allocation/debt normalization rather than replacing it. Serve has broadened delivery channels beyond Uber Eats and expanded vertical scope, but the central expectation gap is still whether deployments convert into durable revenue, utilization and cash economics quickly enough relative to cash burn and dilution capacity.

claims: Teradyne's 2026 TestInsight acquisition and MultiLane Test Products joint venture expand its AI/data-center test stack from design/test software toward high-speed interconnect test, supporting a broader served-market execution thesis.
The company declared a $0.13 quarterly dividend payable September 25, 2026, a modest current capital-return datapoint that does not resolve repurchase, SBC or acquisition-capacity normalization.
risks: AI/data-center served-market expansion may not translate into proportional revenue/margin if customer capex or test intensity disappoints.
Acquisition/JV execution adds integration and capital-allocation complexity.
unknowns: 2026 contribution from TestInsight/MLTP; current repurchase execution; SBC dilution; current debt and acquisition funding capacity.
evidence.exactGate: Do not convert strategic-positioning evidence into an execution score until current 2026 SBC/debt/repurchase normalization is reproducible.

claims: Serve's August 17, 2026 Grubhub/Wonder launch added another delivery-platform path alongside prior Uber Eats and DoorDash relationships and reported more than 2,000 deployed robots and more than 4,000 restaurant relationships.

Serve's March 2026 full-year update guided to approximately $26M of 2026 revenue after 2025 revenue of $2.7M; the magnitude of that growth expectation makes current cash use, financing capacity and realized revenue mix central to execution assessment.
risks: High growth expectations create a wide execution gap if deployments do not monetize at expected utilization and margins.
Cash burn and financing overhang can dominate strategic progress if revenue conversion lags.
Platform diversification does not prove customer/revenue diversification.
contradictions: Broad partnership/deployment narrative is constructive, while the existing underwriting packet still lacks exact current revenue concentration, cash-flow use and equity-overhang extraction needed to quantify economic execution.
unknowns: 2026 YTD revenue versus full-year guidance trajectory; platform/customer revenue mix; robot utilization and contribution margin; H1 operating cash use; unused ATM capacity; warrant/SBC overhang.
evidence.exactGate: Reconcile 2026 revenue trajectory and concentration with Q2 cash-flow/equity-overhang evidence before treating deployment breadth as durable economic execution.
